questions.def: 'Had' begins a conditional inversion, replacing 'If I had known...'
questions.question: ___ I known, I wouldn't have come.

questions.def: 'Which' introduces a non-defining relative clause, adding extra information.
questions.question: The report, ___ I read yesterday, was quite insightful.

questions.def: Passive voice: 'It is said' is the correct passive construction.
questions.question: It is ___ that he will resign.

questions.def: 'Insist' is followed by the preposition 'on' + gerund.
questions.question: She insisted ___ going to the party alone.

questions.def: Inversion is needed after 'Not only' at the beginning of a sentence.
questions.question: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot his wallet.

questions.def: Inversion after 'Little' at the start of a sentence requires auxiliary verb.
questions.question: Little ___ that this would be the last time.

questions.def: 'Despite' introduces a contrast, followed by a gerund phrase.
questions.question: ___ being tired, she finished the project.

questions.def: 'Regret' + gerund (perfect) expresses regret about a past action.
questions.question: He regrets ___ harder in school.

questions.def: 'She is said to be' follows the passive reporting verb structure.
questions.question: She is said ___ a gifted musician.

questions.def: 'Needs' + passive infinitive shows something requires an action.
questions.question: The car needs ___.

questions.def: 'It is time' is followed by the past simple (subjunctive mood).
questions.question: It is time you ___ your own decisions.

questions.def: 'If only' expresses a wish about the present, using past simple.
questions.question: If only I ___ the answer!

questions.def: 'Whose' shows possession in relative clauses.
questions.question: The book, ___ cover is torn, is still readable.

questions.def: Past participle 'read' completes the perfect participle construction 'Having read'.
questions.question: Having ___ all the instructions, he started the machine.

questions.def: 'Is used to' = present habit, so tag question should be 'doesn't she?'
questions.question: She is used to working late, isn't she?

questions.def: 'Wish' about the past uses past perfect: 'I wish you had told'.
questions.question: I wish you ___ me the truth earlier.

questions.def: 'However' introduces a concession, meaning 'no matter how'.
questions.question: ___ hard he tried, he couldn't open the door.

questions.def: 'Is thought to be living' implies a continuous action in the present.
questions.question: She is thought ___ abroad.

questions.def: Avoid 'The reason why... is because...' - redundant use of 'why' and 'because'.
questions.question: The reason why he was late is because he missed the bus.

questions.def: Past participle 'known' completes the perfect participle construction 'Having known'.
questions.question: Having ___ him for years, I trust him completely.

questions.def: Inversion after 'so' requires an adjective: 'So tired did she feel...'
questions.question: So ___ did she feel that she had to leave.

questions.def: After 'essential', use the bare infinitive (subjunctive mood).
questions.question: It is essential that he ___ here tomorrow.

questions.def: Inversion is needed after 'Hardly': 'Hardly had she arrived...'
questions.question: Hardly she had arrived when the phone rang.

questions.def: Passive voice: 'What is done is done' is a common idiom.
questions.question: What ___ is done.

questions.def: 'Regardless' introduces a disregard for something (the cost).
questions.question: ___ of the cost, we decided to go.

questions.def: 'Would rather' is followed by the bare infinitive (without 'to').
questions.question: She would rather ___ home than go to the party.

questions.def: Unless + present simple requires future tense for the main clause.
questions.question: Unless it rains, we ___ for a picnic tomorrow.

questions.def: Participial clause needs subject in main clause to match.
questions.question: Having finished the report, ___.

questions.def: 'Despite' already means 'in spite of', so 'of' is redundant.
questions.question: Despite of the heavy rain, they continued playing.

questions.def: Use passive voice 'is said' for impersonal reports/opinions.
questions.question: It ___ that the company will relocate.
